title: GPU maintenance rotation playbook Q2 2025
body:
Sheet: GPU Maintenance Rotation Playbook - Q2 2025

Purpose:
- Operational playbook for planned driver upgrades and GPU node rotations across regions while keeping per-region capacity above SLO thresholds.
- Prioritize low-risk windows, stagger drains to avoid >12% effective capacity loss in any critical region.

Executive summary:
- Total fleet GPUs: 4,200 (across 6 regions). Baseline fleet utilization (30-day avg): 58% overall; peak hourly 79% (global).
- Target maintenance period: Apr 6 -> Jun 20, 2025. Windows scheduled weekly per region to reduce blast radius.
- Planned activities: node cordon & drain, device driver upgrade (510.x -> 515.x), CUDA runtime validation, node rejoin, post-upgrade stress tests.
- Mitigation: reserved burst pool (220 GPUs) and cross-region temporary routing for non-sensitive traffic.

Capacity impact summary (policy):
- Max allowed planned drain per region at any time: 10% of region GPUs OR 8% of global capacity, whichever is smaller.
- If drain will exceed policy, escalate to on-call infra lead and delay non-critical batches.

Pre-maintenance checklist (run by owner 48->1 hour before window):
- Confirm rolling-compare alert baselines (latency/cost) saved to snapshot.
- Communicate planned drain on #infra-maintenance Slack and to affected product owners.
- Verify reserved burst pool capacity and automation playbooks are healthy.
- Snapshot GPU driver package and current /etc/modprobe configs.
- Confirm build of staging image with new driver installed and smoke test green.

Drain & upgrade steps (per node):
1) Mark node unschedulable: kubectl cordon <node>
2) Drain with graceful eviction: kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120
3) Verify no running infer requests and KV cache persisted if needed.
4) Run host pre-check script (scripts/host_precheck.sh) - GPU health, disk, kernel modules.
5) Stop inference services: systemctl stop redwood-inference.service
6) Install driver: apt install nvidia-driver-515 -y (or yum equivalent)
7) Reboot host and run driver smoke tests: scripts/driver_smoke_test.sh (expected 5 min)
8) Start services and run lightweight endpoint validation against canary prompts.
9) Monitor metrics for 30 minutes: token latency P95, infra errors, GPU utilization.
10) If stable, remove node from maintenance tag and mark schedulable: kubectl uncordon <node>

Rollback criteria and steps:
- Immediate rollback triggers: node fails driver smoke tests, node cannot bind GPU, infra error rate increase >3x baseline, or any failing customer SLA.
- Rollback sequence: reboot into previous kernel/driver (package available in /opt/driver-archive), restore /etc/modprobe.d/ original files, re-run smoke tests. If rollback fails, escalate to on-call kernel team and open INC with priority P0.

Validation & post-upgrade checks (owner):
- Run end-to-end inference smoke suite (20 sample prompts) with golden-output compare.
- Verify KV cache hit ratio within 2 percentage points of baseline.
- Confirm no increase in token generation cost >5% after driver change.
- Confirm alerting thresholds are green for 24 hours before marking window complete.

Monitoring dashboards & thresholds:
- Dashboards: infra/gpu-health, infra/inference-latency, infra/batch-queue-depth.
- Immediate alert: GPU ECC errors > 5/min or new device not appearing.
- High-latency alert: P95 text-gen latency > baseline + 120ms for 15m.

Communication plan:
- Notify #infra-maintenance 72h, 24h, and 1h before window with expected impact numbers.
- During window: periodic updates 30m cadence to the channel.
- Post-window: summary report in Confluence and email to product owners within 6h.

Risk register (top items):
- Risk: Driver incompatibility with custom kernel modules -> Mitigation: test on staging with identical kernel; preserve rollback images.
- Risk: Unexpected capacity shortage due to simultaneous customer load -> Mitigation: pause drains; request auto-burst capacity; re-route non-sensitive traffic.
- Risk: Prolonged node recovery -> Mitigation: remove from rotation and schedule out-of-band replacement; notify impacted customers.

Capacity calculations (example):
- us-east1 pool GPUs: 600. Planned drain 48 GPUs = 8% of pool. Effective remaining capacity = 552 GPUs. With baseline utilization 60% => headroom approx 220 GPUs for peak shift.
- Global reserved burst: 220 GPUs (~5% of fleet) used only if region-level headroom < predicted queue backlog.

Operational notes & heuristics:
- Prefer rolling single-node drains every 6 minutes in larger clusters to preserve KV cache locality.
- Always perform driver upgrades first in staging; then in a small canary (2 nodes) in prod cluster before bulk drain.
- If a region shows error spike during first 30 minutes post-upgrade, pause further drains in that region until mitigation complete.

Open action items (owners):
- Build new driver AMI with 515.x and CUDA runtime (Ethan Morales) - due 2025-03-01
- Add automated smoke test to CI that runs driver validation on every AMI (Hannah Kim) - due 2025-03-10
- Reserve burst pool and validate routing automation (Ava Chen) - due 2025-03-15

Appendix: quick commands
- cordon: kubectl cordon <node>
- drain: kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120
- rejoin: kubectl uncordon <node>
- driver smoke: scripts/driver_smoke_test.sh <node>

Notes to reviewers:
- This sheet is intended to be used by on-call infra engineers and release engineers. Please call out any additional dependencies on dedicated customers (private deployments) so we can schedule separate windows for them.
